blogs.title: The Triple-Stent Dilemma: Navigating TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV Procedures
blogs.description: As TAVI indications expand to younger, lower-risk patients, the era of 'lifetime management' has arrived. This post dissects the rare and complex scenario of a third transcatheter valve implantation (TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV). We analyze the compounding technical challenges of multiple overlapping stent frames, including the risks of severe prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM), reduced effective orifice area, and the critical importance of commissural alignment to preserve future coronary access. Using a recent case of a patient surviving three sequential implants, we outline the strategic planning required to avoid turning the aortic root into an impenetrable fortress.

blogs.title: To Cut or to Cath? Managing Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis in the Prohibitive Surgical Candidate
blogs.description: Current guidelines strongly favor surgical explantation for prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE), especially when structural deterioration follows infection. But what happens when the surgical risk is prohibitive (EuroSCORE II >27%) due to comorbidities and prior complex interventions? This post explores the controversial but increasingly necessary role of TAVI as a salvage therapy for treated PVE. We discuss the criteria for proceeding—specifically confirming eradication of infection via TEE and CT—and weigh the risks of seeding a new valve against the certainty of mortality without intervention.

blogs.title: Beyond the Echo: Why MSCT is Non-Negotiable in Complex Valve Reinterventions
blogs.description: In standard TAVI, echocardiography often leads the way, but in multi-layered redo procedures, it simply isn't enough. This deep dive highlights how Multislice CT (MSCT) becomes the primary roadmap for TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV cases. We examine specific imaging metrics that dictate success: measuring minimum lumen diameters through existing stents, calculating virtual valve-to-coronary distances to predict obstruction, and modeling 'neo-skirt' formation. Learn how precise CT-guided planning allows operators to select implant depths that maximize hemodynamics while keeping coronary ostia accessible despite layers of metal mesh.

blogs.title: Chasing Gradients: Understanding and Mitigating Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch in Redo TAVI
blogs.description: A immediate post-procedure mean gradient of 67 mmHg sounds like a disaster, yet this patient improved rapidly to normal function within a month. This post analyzes the phenomenon of acute versus subacute hemodynamic improvement in nested valve procedures. We discuss the mechanisms behind severe initial prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) caused by leaflet immobilization and frame constraint, and how high-pressure post-dilation and tissue remodeling over time can rescue effective orifice area. Key takeaways include recognizing when high gradients are transient versus when they signal true failure.

blogs.title: Device Selection Strategy: Choosing the Right Tool for a Crowded Aortic Root
blogs.description: Not all valves are created equal when space is at a premium. In this case study, the team chose a self-expanding supra-annular valve (Acurate neo2) over other options for the third implant. Why? This post breaks down the biomechanical rationale for device selection in tight anatomies, focusing on frame height, radial force, and leaflet positioning. We compare how different platform designs interact with previous generations of valves (e.g., Lotus and Evolut) and why specific features like low-profile frames and commissural alignment capabilities are essential for preventing coronary occlusion in triple-stent scenarios.
